title: Probability outside a Fourier family
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to the signs, and let $\\mathcal F$ be any family of subsets of the coordinate set. The probability that a spectral sample of $f$ lies outside $\\mathcal F$ equals the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ over subsets outside $\\mathcal F$.
hypotheses_covered: arbitrary family $\\mathcal F$ of coordinate subsets
